# Teleport and Phase Shift: Recharge System (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

## Problem statement

Teleport and Phase Shift charges are consumed on use and never replenish, making them one-shot abilities. Both should recharge over a configurable period so charges return to a capped pool, with recharge time reduced at higher levels.

## Users

- **Primary player:** needs a safety net that recovers over time — a consumed escape should return rather than being gone forever.
- **Secondary player:** upgrade decisions should feel impactful; reduced recharge time is a meaningful progression incentive.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Per-charge recharge model:** each consumed charge of Phase Shift and Teleport independently starts a recharge timer. When the timer elapses the charge returns to the pool. A consumed charge that has been recharged and spent again starts a new timer.
- **Maximum charge cap of 3:** the pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability, whether collected (field pickup / hold-full reward) or recharged. Any collection or recharge that would exceed the cap is discarded.
- **Level-up reduces recharge time:** a new level variable `phaseRechargeTime` (seconds, exponential-saturation curve, e.g. base 30 s → cap 10 s) for Phase Shift and `teleportRechargeTime` (e.g. base 15 s → cap 5 s) — recharge time is level-derived. Higher levels = shorter recharge.
- **Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool:** the hold-full reward no longer grants unlimited activations; it adds one charge (up to the cap of 3) and recharges like any other charge.
- **HUD greys out unavailable items:** when a power-up has zero available charges, its HUD row (icon + label + value) is rendered greyed-out/inactive. When charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- **Field pickup grants one charge:** collecting Phase Shift or Teleport from the field grants one charge (level-derived via `phaseCharges` / `teleportStacks` from the level catalogue, clamped so total never exceeds 3).
- **All tests pass** with no build warnings — the full project test suite (`npm test`) and typecheck (`npm run typecheck`) both pass with the new changes.
- **Documentation updated** — the Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections, power-up levelling section) and relevant code comments are updated to describe the recharge model; the CHANGELOG is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded.

## Constraints

- Existing level curve infrastructure (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/utils/curve.ts`) must be reused — no new curve implementation.
- `PowerUpLevelStore` stack semantics must remain single-source-of-truth.
- Gym scenes must inherit the behaviour identically (gym ↔ game parity).
- PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN (0.5 s shared governor for danger-triggered activations) remains unchanged.
- Recharge timers are run-scoped: they reset with the level store on run restart (weapon-parity, `PowerUpLevelStore.reset()`).
- Recharge timers tick while the game runs; no explicit pause-behaviour requirement (timers may pause with the scene — acceptable default, flagged for review).

## Existing state

- **Phase Shift** (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `PowerUpLevelStore._phaseCharges`): stores a count of auto-activation charges. `consumePhaseCharge()` decrements; permanent grants `isPhasePermanent() === true` and bypasses the count.
- **Teleport** (`src/powerups/effects.ts`, `PowerUpLevelStore._teleportStacks`): stores FIFO uses. `consumeTeleport()` decrements.
- **Level catalogue** (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`): levels `phaseCharges` (1→3) and `teleportStacks` (1→3) via exponential-saturation curves. These represent *grant per pickup*, not pool size.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`): rows hidden when charge count = 0. Icons use `ICON_COLORS` (Phase Shift = grey `0xaaaaaa`, Teleport = orange).
- **No recharge mechanism exists.** Charges are consumed permanently.

## Desired change

- Replace the binary "has-charge / no-charge" model with a **per-charge recharge timer**.
- Introduce level variables for recharge time in the existing level catalogue.
- Apply the same cap-of-3 logic to both field-granted and permanently-granted charges.
- Grey-out HUD rows when the pool is empty.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — add `phaseRechargeTime`, `teleportRechargeTime` level specs; update `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — introduce per-charge recharge timers in `EffectsRegistry`; modify `consumePhaseCharge` / `consumeTeleport` to start timers.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — inject `PowerUpLevelStore` and tick recharge timers.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — detect zero-charges state and render greyed-out row.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — possibly add a grey-out variant for power-up icons.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.test.ts` / `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — recharge timer tests, cap-3 enforcement, level-derived recharge time, permanent Phase Shift as pool.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance risk:** the permanent Phase Shift reward is nerfed (unlimited → capped recharging pool). Mitigation: cap is deliberately 3 and recharge time is level-reducible; flagged for producer awareness.
- **Integration risk:** the shared automatic-defence resolver (`_updateAutoDefence`) selects between Phase Shift and Teleport based on available counts; with recharge, an empty pool contributes zero available count. Verify resolver ties/ordering still hold when both pools are partially charged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** related but out-of-scope opportunities (e.g. a visible recharge countdown bar, audio cues for recharge-complete, gym-specific recharge sliders) should be recorded as linked work items, not folded into this brief.
- **Assumption:** recharge time values (Phase 30 s → 10 s; Teleport 15 s → 5 s) are proposed defaults; exact base/cap/k are tunable during planning/implementation and must be re-confirmed if the producer prefers different pacing.

## Related work

- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Power-up level curve catalogue (parent for all level variables).
- AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8 — Phase Shift automatic activation (parent for Phase Shift behaviour).
- AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC — Teleport automatic activation (parent for Teleport behaviour).
- AH-0MUX96GJF006CAZP — Enable mineral collection between waves.
- AH-0MUHMXWGC0058BO4 — Hold-full rewards in gyms.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should 'recharge' mean — per-charge cooldown, one shared cooldown, or other?" — Answer (producer): "(A) Per-charge cooldown — each consumed charge refills independently; a pool of N collected charges returns to N available. Recharge starts when a charge is spent." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Where is the 'upgrades list' that greys out?" — Answer (producer): "(A) HUD effect rows — the player's owned power-up list on the left stays visible but greys the row + icon while no charge is available." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Permanent Phase Shift interaction — keep unlimited, or make it a recharging pool?" — Answer (producer): "(B) It should be the ONLY recharge model. When picked up during play that is a single (stacking) charge. Once used it is gone. The recharges can stack too, up to a maximum of 3 (for both collected and recharged)." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** – Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD (interactions, impacts, enemy actions, advanced telegraphing) (completed)
- **AH-0MUICQBE5007AIRU** – Add enemy-gym phase/shield gating regression tests (completed)
- **AH-0MV39AQOY006I083** – Update campaign documentation for 10-level structure (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muhmxwgc0058bo4, 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mux96gjf006cazp, 0muze4aip009hzwc (+276 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0muu2qje2007jnr6, 0mux96gjf006cazp, 0muze4aip009hzwc, ability (+263 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0muhmxwgc0058bo4, 0muiyx1ee008fvs8, 0mux96gjf006cazp, ability, add (+224 more)
## Plan (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

Decomposed into **10 child features** (test/verification-first, dependency
ordered) plus **3 recorded out-of-scope follow-ups** (sibling items,
`discovered-from:AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR`).

1. **Unit tests: recharge-time level axes** (task, tests-first for #2) — verify
   `phaseRechargeRate` / `teleportRechargeRate` resolution, monotonicity, caps,
   time inverse (30→10 s / 15→5 s) and change-summary deltas. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
2. **Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue** (feature) — add the
   two rate axes (base→cap: Phase 1/30→1/10, Teleport 1/15→1/5 charges/s),
   stats/resolver exposure, seconds inverse, change summary; GDD §4.4
   levelling table row. Dep: #1. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, GDD.
3. **Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3** (task, tests-first for
   #4) — independent per-charge timers, cap-of-3 for collected/recharged,
   level-derived recharge time, permanent Phase Shift as pool, reset().
   Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
4. **Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore** (feature) — per-charge
   recharge timers + `tickRecharge(dt)`, cap-3 clamping on collect/recharge,
   `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()`, permanent Phase Shift =
   recharging pool (+1 clamped), hold-full Teleport +1, run-scoped reset.
   Dep: #3. Files: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`.
5. **Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, scene parity** (task,
   tests-first for #6) — registry tick advances recharge, finite-pool
   `selectAutoDefence` (no Infinity), partial-pool tie/ordering, game↔gym
   parity through the shared tick path. Files: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
6. **Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence** (feature) —
   `EffectsRegistry.tick` advances store recharge timers; `selectAutoDefence`
   finite capped pools; empty pool contributes zero available count;
   PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN unchanged. Dep: #5. Files: `src/powerups/effects.ts`.
7. **Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools** (task, tests-first for #8)
   — owned-but-empty Phase Shift/Teleport pool renders a greyed row; >0 renders
   normal; not-owned hidden; label counts recharge-aware. Files: `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`.
8. **HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows** (feature) — greyed row
   (icon + label + value) when owned pool is empty; shared grey icon variant in
   `icons.ts`; row stays visible (not hidden). Dep: #7. Files: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
   `src/powerups/icons.ts`.
9. **Document the recharge model (GDD + code comments)** (docs) — update GDD
   teleport/phase-shift sections, power-up levelling + HUD presentation, and
   module headers; no longer claim unlimited permanent activations. Dep: #8.
   Files: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`.
10. **Verify full suite + typecheck pass with recharge changes** (task,
    final gate for parent AC7) — `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` both pass;
    parity sweep green. Dep: #8, #9.

Test-first ordering guarantee: every implementation feature has its test item
created before it and dependency-wired (test → impl per feature; impl chain
#2→#4→#6→#8 carries the model forward).

## Plan Appendix (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR)

- Q: "Recharge-time curve encoding — the brief's AC3 specifies a *decreasing*
  `phaseRechargeTime` (30 s → 10 s), but the shared exponential-saturation curve
  (`curveValue`) pins inverted specs flat at base, and the catalogue enforces a
  monotonic non-decreasing invariant (tests, parent AC4 of AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6).
  **Recommended:** (A) store increasing rates `phaseRechargeRate` /
  `teleportRechargeRate` (charges/s, Phase 1/30→1/10, Teleport 1/15→1/5) and
  expose the AC's seconds at point of use (`1/rate` → 30→10 s, 15→5 s),
  mirroring the `bombFrequency`/`bombInterval` precedent and reusing the curve
  with no new implementation." — Answer (operator): "1. A" (A). Final: A.
  Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.
- Q: "Field-pickup grant size — AC6 says field pickup "grants one charge"
  (level-derived via `phaseCharges`/`teleportStacks` from the catalogue,
  clamped ≤ 3). **Recommended:** (A) grant the level-derived count (1 at base
  level → up to 3), total clamped to 3, preserving the "grant per pickup"
  catalogue semantics described in the brief's Existing-state section." —
  Answer (operator): "2. A" (A). Final: A. Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.
- Q: "Teleport hold-full reward — the ACs redefine the Phase Shift permanent
  reward (permanent → +1 recharging charge ≤ 3) but are silent on the Teleport
  hold-full reward (today grants the level-derived stacks on a permanent grant).
  **Recommended:** (A) mirror Phase Shift — hold-full Teleport grants +1 charge
  (clamped ≤ 3) and recharges normally, keeping both defensive pools symmetric
  for the shared auto-defence resolver." — Answer (operator): "3. A" (A).
  Final: A. Source: interactive reply, plan round 1.

# Unit tests: recharge-time level axes

## Goal

Verify the new recharge-time level axes resolve correctly before implementation (test-first; drives the catalogue implementation feature). A player's recharge time is level-derived; these tests pin the maths so the later engine and HUD work on a verified foundation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `phaseRechargeRate` and `teleportRechargeRate` resolve deterministically from `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at every level 0..8, monotonic non-decreasing and clamped to their caps (Phase Shift base 1/30 → cap 1/10 charges/s; Teleport base 1/15 → cap 1/5).
- Level-up reduces recharge time: the seconds inverse (`1/rate`) decreases with level — 30 → 10 s for Phase Shift and 15 → 5 s for Teleport — and a higher level never recharges slower than a lower level.
- `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` reports a positive delta for the rate axes between levels (using the catalogue label/unit) and omits them once the curve has flattened.
- The axes are members of `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` in catalogue order; the existing catalogue-completeness and monotonicity suites still pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` with a recharge-axes describe block (resolution, monotonicity, caps, seconds inverse, change-summary deltas).
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — the suite stays red until the implementation feature lands.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first item; the implementation feature is dependency-wired to this item).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts

# Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue

## Goal

Add the two recharge-time axes to the single power-up level catalogue (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6), reusing the shared exponential-saturation curve — no new curve implementation. Producer decision (plan Q1): the axes are stored as increasing **rates** (charges/s) so the monotonic non-decreasing invariant holds; the AC's seconds are exposed at point of use as `1/rate`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New level variables `phaseRechargeRate` (base 1/30 → cap 1/10 charges/s) and `teleportRechargeRate` (base 1/15 → cap 1/5) exist in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` with label/unit/description/rationale, resolved through the shared exponential-saturation curve — no new curve implementation.
- Level-up reduces recharge time: `phaseRechargeTime()` and `teleportRechargeTime()` (the seconds inverse `1/rate`) decrease with level — 30 → 10 s for Phase Shift and 15 → 5 s for Teleport — recharge time is level-derived and higher levels recharge faster.
- `PowerUpLevelVariable`, `PowerUpLevelStats` and `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` include the new axes; both resolve monotonic non-decreasing and clamped to cap; neither is listed in `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES`.
- `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` surfaces the rate deltas in the hold-full change summary.
- The GDD power-up levelling table (§4.4) lists the two new axes with their base/cap values.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`: variable-type union and `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` order, `PowerUpLevelStats` fields, two specs in the phase_shift / teleport buckets, resolver exposure.
- Add seconds accessors on the store/stats path (`1/rate`) — the API surface for the recharge engine.
- Update `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 levelling table.

## Dependencies

- Unit tests: recharge-time level axes (test-first).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts
- docs/Game Design Document.md

# Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3

## Goal

Verify the run-scoped per-charge recharge model in `PowerUpLevelStore` before implementation (test-first; drives the engine implementation feature). Covers independent per-charge timers, the cap-of-3, level-derived recharge time, and the permanent Phase Shift reward as a recharging pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each consumed charge of Phase Shift and Teleport independently starts a recharge timer; advancing recharge time returns the charge to the pool; a charge that has recharged and been spent again starts a fresh timer.
- The pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability — whether collected (field pickup or hold-full reward) or recharged — and any excess grant/recharge is discarded.
- Recharge time is level-derived via the rate axes: `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()` reflect the level, so higher levels recharge faster.
- Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool (no unlimited activations): `isPhasePermanent()` no longer implies unbounded consumption; the hold-full reward adds one charge (≤ 3, clamped) that recharges like any other.
- Teleport hold-full mirrors Phase Shift: +1 charge (≤ 3, clamped), recharging normally.
- `reset()` clears all recharge timers and both charge pools (run restart, weapon parity).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` with recharge describe blocks (independent timers, clamp 3, level-derived time, permanent-as-pool, reset).
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — red until the engine implementation lands.

## Dependencies

- Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue (the axes must exist to assert level-derived times).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts

# Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore

## Goal

Implement the run-scoped per-charge recharge model in the single `PowerUpLevelStore`: every consumed Phase Shift / Teleport charge starts its own timer and returns when the level-derived time elapses, capped at 3, and the permanent Phase Shift hold-full reward is converted from unlimited activations to a recharging pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-charge recharge model: `consumePhaseCharge()` / `consumeTeleport()` start one independent recharge timer per consumed charge; when the level-derived time elapses the charge returns to the pool; a charge that has recharged and been spent again starts a new timer.
- Maximum charge cap of 3: the pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability, whether collected (field pickup / hold-full reward) or recharged. Any collection or recharge that would exceed the cap is discarded.
- Level-up reduces recharge time: recharge time is level-derived via `phaseRechargeRate`/`teleportRechargeRate`; `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()` expose seconds (`1/rate`) so higher levels recharge faster.
- Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool: the hold-full reward no longer grants unlimited activations; it adds one charge (up to the cap of 3) and recharges like any other charge.
- Field pickup grants one charge: collecting Phase Shift or Teleport from the field grants the level-derived grant count (`phaseCharges`/`teleportStacks` from the level catalogue), clamped so the total never exceeds 3.
- Teleport hold-full mirrors Phase Shift: +1 charge, clamped to 3, recharging normally.
- Recharge timers are run-scoped: they advance while the game runs and are cleared by `reset()` with the level store (weapon parity).

## Minimal Implementation

- `PowerUpLevelStore`: per-charge recharge-timer state, `tickRecharge(dt)`, grant/consume clamping (collect field/hold-full, recharge-complete), seconds accessors, redefinition of `_phasePermanent` as an owned flag (not unlimited), `reset()` clearing.
- Update module-header docs to describe the recharge model.

## Dependencies

- Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3 (test-first).
- Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue (axes + seconds accessors).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts

# Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity

## Goal

Verify the recharge wiring through the shared tick path, the finite-pool automatic-defence resolver, and game↔gym parity before implementing the wiring (test-first; drives the wiring implementation feature).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected level store's recharge timers so depleted Phase Shift/Teleport pools recover over time.
- `selectAutoDefence` with finite capped pools: the greater available count wins, an exact tie uses the injected-RNG 50/50, `null` when both pools are empty, and partial (mid-recharge) pools order exactly per the parent resolver rule — with no unbounded/permanent-Infinity branch.
- `updateDanger` spends a defence only when the selected pool is non-empty; an empty pool contributes zero available count.
- Scene parity: the recharge advance runs through the shared registry tick consumed by PlayScene, GymFormationScene and GymPowerUpsCombat; the duplicate-body guard / equivalence suite still passes (gym ↔ game parity).
- HUD-facing accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) report recharge-aware values.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (tick-advances-recharge, finite-pool resolver, updateDanger) and the parity suites (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`) where the recharge path is exercised.
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — red until the wiring implementation lands.

## Dependencies

- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore (the engine must exist to tick).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.test.ts
- src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts

# Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence

## Goal

Advance the store's recharge timers from the shared registry tick (the one path every scene consumes, guaranteeing parity) and convert the automatic-defence resolver from the old unlimited-permanent model to finite capped pools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected store's recharge timers (shared tick path → identical behaviour in the game and every gym).
- `selectAutoDefence` no longer treats any pool as unbounded: both Phase Shift and Teleport are finite pools capped at 3; ordering by greater available count and the exact-tie RNG branch are unchanged; the permanent-Phase-Shift-Infinity branch is removed.
- `updateDanger` selects a defence only when the pool is non-empty (an empty pool contributes zero available count); the shared re-arm governor and `PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN` (0.5 s) are unchanged.
- Registry accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) reflect recharge state for the HUD.
- No gameplay divergence between the game and the gyms (shared registry tick + shared resolver, duplicate-body guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/powerups/effects.ts`: tick wiring, `selectAutoDefence` signature/body (drop the permanent-Infinity semantics), HUD accessors, header docs.
- `CombatScene._updateAutoDefence` and the scene tick sites consume the registry unchanged (verify no edits needed).

## Dependencies

- Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity (test-first).
- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore.

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.ts

# HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows

## Goal

When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, render its HUD row (icon + label + value) greyed-out/inactive instead of hiding it; render normally when charges > 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, its HUD row is rendered greyed-out/inactive; when charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- Row visibility: an owned Phase Shift/Teleport with an empty pool stays visible (greyed), not hidden; power-ups the player has never owned stay hidden.
- The icon, label and value share one greyed styling derived from a shared grey variant (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), so icon and text cannot diverge.
- Charged rows and all non-charge rows render unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/ui/HUD.ts`: `_isPowerUpRowVisible` / `_powerUpStacks` (owned-but-empty → visible + greyed), `_addRow` grey styling, HUD docs.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`: shared grey variant for the Phase Shift/Teleport icons used by the HUD.

## Dependencies

- Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools (test-first).
- Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence.

## Key Files

- src/ui/HUD.ts
- src/powerups/icons.ts

# Document the recharge model (GDD + code comments)

## Goal

Bring the Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections, power-up levelling section, HUD presentation) and the relevant code comments up to date with the recharge model, so the written design matches the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections and the power-up levelling section) and relevant code comments are updated to describe the recharge model; the CHANGELOG is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded.
- The teleport and phase-shift sections of the Game Design Document describe recharging charge pools (per-charge timers, cap of 3, level-derived recharge time) and no longer claim unlimited activations for the permanent Phase Shift reward.
- The GDD power-up levelling section (§4.4) and HUD presentation describe the new recharge-time axes and the greyed-out-row behaviour for zero-charge pools.
- Relevant code comments in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and `src/powerups/effects.ts` (module headers, consume/collect/resolver docs) match the recharge model.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit `docs/Game Design Document.md` (teleport/phase-shift sections, power-up levelling + HUD presentation) and the two module header/comment blocks.
